This is first application under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973 for grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant who has been arrested relating to FIR/Crime No.258/2023 dated 16.07.2023 registered at Police Station Khamariya, District Jabalpur (M.P.) for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 376(2) of IPC and Sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 5(L) of the POCSO Act (as mentioned in the application).
2 . Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is in custody since 18.07.2023 and the trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that the applicant is innocent and has falsely been implicated in the case.
The applicant is a permanent resident of district and there is no possibility of his absconding or tampering with prosecution evidence.

He is ready to Vipin Yadav vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158324757/
1 furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the conditions to be imposed by the Court.

sentences.text: Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.
3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
5.
The DNA report is not received yet.
6. Learned counsel for the applicant has argued the bail application on the basis of statements of prosecutrix and her parents recorded before the trial Court.

The Class-X mark-sheet of prosecutrix was seized in the matter in which her date of birth is mentioned as 19.10.2007, while the FIR reveals that the date of incident was 14.02.2023, therefore, she was below 16 years at the time of incident.

It is emphasized by counsel for the applicant that all the three witnesses examined before the trial Court have denied the correctness of date of birth mentioned in Class-X mark-sheet, but this Court is not inclined to evaluate that evidence while deciding this bail application.
7. Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands dismissed.
